tagline: Leading regulated utility focused on sustainable infrastructure investment and carbon-free nuclear generation
hero_kpi_rationale: Regulated Rate Base is a key indicator of the company's growth and stability, as it reflects the value of regulated assets that generate sustainable and predictable revenues.

kpis.name: Regulated Rate Base
kpis.explanation: Value of regulated assets that generate revenues for the company
kpis.description: PEG's regulated rate base increased 5.9% in 2025, rising from $34 billion in 2024 to $36 billion in 2025, reflecting the company's investments in regulated assets and approval of working capital recovery in distribution rate proceedings.

kpis.name: Capital Investment Program
kpis.explanation: Planned capital investments in regulated assets over the 2026-2030 period
kpis.description: PEG plans to invest between $22.5 billion and $25.5 billion in regulated assets between 2026 and 2030 to modernize energy infrastructure, improve reliability, and meet growing energy demand.
kpis.signal: Significant capital investments for modernization and reliability

risks.title: Risk of loss of ROE outperformance premium
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned in the 'Transmission Rate Proceedings and Return on Equity' section; loss of 50 basis point premium could reduce annual net income by $40 million; language indicates clear prospective impact; heavily weighted regulatory category; risk stable compared to prior year.

risks.title: Uncertainty on nuclear production tax credits (PTC)
risks.score_rationale: PTC is central to nuclear profitability; uncertainty regarding revenue thresholds and US Treasury guidance is explicitly emphasized; retroactive adjustments possible; existential impact on PSEG Power strategy; strengthened new risk in 2025.

risks.title: Litigation related to Long Island contract renewal
risks.score_rationale: A competitor appealed after rejection of its complaint on the procurement process; mentioned in recent developments; moderate intensity language; limited legal risk but potentially costly; new development in 2026.

risks.title: Risks related to environmental regulation at Newark Bay
risks.score_rationale: Present in the 'Environmental Regulation' section; Superfund designation by EPA; potential liability for significant remediation costs; longstanding but persistent risk; explicit mention of potentially material costs.

risks.title: Capacity supply tensions in PJM
risks.score_rationale: Capacity prices surged in 2024-2025; risk of regulatory instability and tariff pressure; mention of 'reliability backstop auction' in preparation; alarmist language on supply-demand imbalances; existential risk to supply security.

risks.title: Possible delay on Maryland-Virginia transmission project
risks.score_rationale: $424 million project threatened by Maryland regulatory delays; 2027 in-service date deemed unrealistic; mention of 'cannot predict the outcome'; moderate operational risk but with potential financial impact.

risks.title: Uncertain evolution of New Jersey energy policy
risks.score_rationale: New administration in 2026; uncertainty regarding implementation of Energy Master Plan; possible changes to decarbonization targets; direct impact on planned investments; elevated strategic risk.

risks.title: Dependence on nuclear support policies
risks.score_rationale: PSEG depends on policies such as ZEC and PTC to maintain nuclear economic viability; explicit mention of ZEC abandonment in favor of PTC; risk of withdrawal or modification of incentives; language emphasizing strategic importance; existential risk for PSEG Power.

ai_positioning.summary: PEG does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K report. The information provided focuses primarily on financial aspects, operations, and business-related risks, with no reference to AI or related technology.
